summary_paragraph: A woman with advanced AIDS (CD4 ~14–16, recently restarted HAART), ESRD on thrice-weekly hemodialysis, and prior V1 herpes zoster ophthalmicus with chronic post-herpetic neuralgia and right-eye visual loss was admitted with worsening right facial pain, pruritic ulcerative facial lesions, and increased headaches with intermittent photophobia. She was initially treated empirically with IV acyclovir while Dermatology and Infectious Disease evaluated for zoster reactivation; ophthalmology found no dendritic corneal involvement. Skin viral testing was negative for HSV/VZV, and punch biopsies of the left arm and right face showed a hypersensitivity/eosinophilic dermatitis consistent with eosinophilic folliculitis; acyclovir was stopped and topical mupirocin plus hydroxyzine were used with improvement in lesions and symptoms. Headache evaluation included CT head, fluoroscopy-guided lumbar puncture, and non-contrast MRI brain, all without evidence of intracranial infection or acute process; CSF studies were reassuring with HSV/VZV negative. She continued HAART and opportunistic infection prophylaxis (TMP-SMX and azithromycin), received hemodialysis during admission with renal management including increased sevelamer dosing, and had a brief self-resolving episode of atrial fibrillation with RVR while continuing aspirin. She was discharged home with services, instructions for suture removal, continuation of dialysis and medications, and outpatient follow-up for ongoing neuropathic facial pain and HIV care.
